title: Inverse-Root Support, Polynomial Amplitudes, and Laurent Moment Channels

claims.statement: For every complex polynomial P, the fixed-seed cyclic rank equals the nonzero inverse-residue support size and the reduced constant span dimension of its generic inverse roots.
Relative to named imported classifications, Theorem 11.1 gives the complete all-degree coefficient atlas for complex polynomial phases of fixed-seed cyclic rank at most three.
Relative to the same inputs, Sections 7 through 10 classify every proper rank-preserving polynomial extension of an Atlas phase.

For every polynomial phase P and polynomial amplitude A dx with primitive G, the amplitude cyclic rank equals the non-trace inverse support size of G and the reduced constant span dimension of the values G(x_j).
The polynomial-amplitude cyclic rank is zero exactly when its primitive G belongs to C[P].
Vanishing on a specified zero-dimensional cycle is equivalent to Fourier annihilation on every active primitive-amplitude channel.
The endpoint table classifies persistent polynomial moments for every phase in the q(P) at most three Atlas.
For every Laurent phase with zero-pole order m and every Laurent amplitude A dz, its kth residue moment is the tau to the mk minus 1 coefficient of A(phi(tau)) phi prime(tau).
A finite zero prefix proves persistent Laurent moment vanishing.
Every persistent Laurent solution is a composition solution.
The candidate is externally refereed, independently reproduced, fully formalised, or priority-certified.
The package gives a finite normal-form classification for all Laurent phase-amplitude pairs.
